metadata.title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
metadata.authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos and Stephen Bates

nodes.name: Marginal coverage
nodes.statement: A prediction set $\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})$ has marginal coverage at level $1-\alpha$ if $1-\alpha \leq \mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})) \leq 1-\alpha+\frac{1}{n+1}$, with probability marginal over calibration and test randomness.

nodes.name: Conformal score function
nodes.statement: A conformal (nonconformity) score is a function $s(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}$ where larger values encode worse agreement between $x$ and $y$.

nodes.name: Conformal quantile $\hat{q}$
nodes.statement: $\hat{q}$ is the $\frac{\lceil (n+1)(1-\alpha) \rceil}{n}$ empirical quantile of calibration scores $s_1,\dots,s_n$.

nodes.name: Split conformal prediction set
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) = \{y : s(X_{\rm test},y) \le \hat{q}\}$.

nodes.name: Conditional coverage
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{C}$ has conditional coverage at level $1-\alpha$ if $\mathbb{P}\left[Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid X_{\rm test}\right] \geq 1-\alpha$ for every value of $X_{\rm test}$.

nodes.name: Feature-stratified coverage (FSC) metric
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{FSC} = \min_{g} \frac{1}{|\mathcal{I}_g|} \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}_g} \mathbf{1}\{Y_i^{\rm (val)} \in \mathcal{C}(X_i^{\rm (val)})\}$, the worst-group coverage over discrete feature groups.

nodes.name: Size-stratified coverage (SSC) metric
nodes.statement: Same as FSC but $\mathcal{I}_g$ groups validation examples by binned set-size $|\mathcal{C}(x)|$ rather than by feature group.

nodes.name: Group-balanced coverage
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}\left( Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid X_{\rm test,1}=g \right) \geq 1-\alpha$ for all groups $g \in \{1,\dots,G\}$.

nodes.name: Class-balanced (class-conditional) coverage
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}\left( Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid Y_{\rm test}=y \right) \geq 1-\alpha$ for all classes $y \in \{1,\dots,K\}$.

nodes.name: Conformal risk control guarantee
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}\left[ \ell(\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}), Y_{\rm test}) \right] \leq \alpha$ for a bounded loss $\ell$ that shrinks as $\mathcal{C}$ grows; recovers miscoverage when $\ell = \mathbf{1}\{Y \notin \mathcal{C}\}$.

nodes.name: Covariate shift
nodes.statement: Distribution shift where $X_{\rm test} \sim \mathcal{P}_{\rm test}$ differs from calibration $X \sim \mathcal{P}$, while the conditional $\mathcal{P}_{Y|X}$ stays fixed.

nodes.name: Likelihood-ratio weight $w(x)$
nodes.statement: $w(x) = \mathrm{d}\mathcal{P}_{\rm test}(x)/\mathrm{d}\mathcal{P}(x)$, the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the test distribution w.r.t. the calibration distribution.

nodes.name: Effective sample size $n^{\rm eff}$
nodes.statement: $n^{\rm eff}(w_1,\dots,w_n) = (\sum w_i)^2/\sum w_i^2$; characterizes the variance penalty of weighting.

nodes.name: Bernoulli sequence (Kolmogorov)
nodes.statement: A deterministic binary sequence of length $n$ with $k$ ones is Bernoulli if it is `random' in the set of $\binom{n}{k}$ such sequences, where random means Kolmogorov complexity close to $\log\binom{n}{k}$.

nodes.name: Risk control property (RCP)
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 Instructions for Learn then Test
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}_{\hat{\lambda}}$ is an $(\alpha,\delta)$-risk-controlling prediction if $\mathbb{P}(R(\hat{\lambda}) \leq \alpha) \geq 1-\delta$, where $\hat{\lambda}$ depends on the calibration data.

nodes.name: Familywise-error rate (FWER)
nodes.section: Appendix A.1.2 Crash Course on FWER
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{FWER}(\hat{\Lambda}) = \mathbb{P}(\exists \hat{\lambda} \in \hat{\Lambda} : R(\hat{\lambda}) > \alpha)$, the probability of at least one false rejection.

nodes.name: P-value (super-uniformity)
nodes.section: Appendix A.1.1 Crash Course on Generating p-values
nodes.statement: A statistic $p_\lambda$ is a valid p-value for null $\mathcal{H}_\lambda$ if $\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{H}_\lambda}(p_\lambda \leq t) \leq t$ for all $t \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Pinball (quantile) loss
nodes.statement: $L_\gamma(\hat{t}_\gamma,y) = (y-\hat{t}_\gamma)\gamma\,\mathbf{1}\{y > \hat{t}_\gamma\} + (\hat{t}_\gamma-y)(1-\gamma)\,\mathbf{1}\{y \leq \hat{t}_\gamma\}$.

nodes.name: Beta distribution of conformal coverage
nodes.section: 3.2 Effect of the Size of the Calibration Set
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid \{(X_i,Y_i)\}_{i=1}^n) \sim \mathrm{Beta}(n+1-l,\,l)$ where $l = \lfloor(n+1)\alpha\rfloor$.

nodes.name: Hoeffding p-value
nodes.section: Appendix A.1.1 Crash Course on Generating p-values
nodes.statement: $p_\lambda^{\rm Hoeffding} = e^{-2n(\alpha-\hat{R}(\lambda))_+^2}$, where $\hat{R}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i L(\mathcal{T}_\lambda(X_i),Y_i)$.

nodes.name: Hoeffding-Bentkus (HB) p-value
nodes.section: Appendix A.1.1 Crash Course on Generating p-values
nodes.statement: $p_\lambda^{\rm HB} = \min(\exp\{-n h_1(\hat{R}(\lambda) \wedge \alpha,\alpha)\},\, e\,\mathbb{P}(\mathrm{Bin}(n,\alpha) \leq \lceil n\hat{R}(\lambda)\rceil))$ with $h_1(a,b) = a\log(a/b) + (1-a)\log((1-a)/(1-b))$.

nodes.name: Conformal coverage guarantee (Vovk-Gammerman-Saunders)
nodes.statement: If $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1,\dots,n}$ and $(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are i.i.d., $\hat{q}$ is as in step 3 and $\mathcal{C}$ as in step 4, then $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})) \geq 1-\alpha$.
assumptions: $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1,\dots,n}$ and $(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are i.i.d. (or exchangeable)
$\hat{q}$ is the $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n$ empirical quantile of calibration scores

nodes.name: Conformal calibration upper bound
nodes.statement: If additionally the scores $s_1,\dots,s_n$ have a continuous joint distribution, then $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test},U_{\rm test},\hat{q})) \leq 1-\alpha+\frac{1}{n+1}$.
assumptions: Scores $s_1,\dots,s_n$ have a continuous joint distribution

nodes.name: Error control for group-balanced conformal prediction
nodes.statement: If $(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_n,Y_n),(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are i.i.d., then the group-stratified conformal set $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid X_{\rm test,1}=g) \geq 1-\alpha$ for every group $g$.
assumptions: $\hat{q}^{(g)}$ computed within each group as the $\lceil(n^{(g)}+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n^{(g)}$ quantile of group-$g$ scores
conclusions: $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid X_{\rm test,1}=g) \geq 1-\alpha$ for all $g$

nodes.name: Error control for class-balanced conformal prediction
nodes.statement: If $(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_n,Y_n),(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are i.i.d., then the class-stratified conformal set satisfies $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid Y_{\rm test}=y) \geq 1-\alpha$ for all $y \in \{1,\dots,K\}$.
assumptions: $\hat{q}^{(k)}$ computed within each class as the $\lceil(n^{(k)}+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n^{(k)}$ quantile of class-$k$ scores
conclusions: $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) \mid Y_{\rm test}=y) \geq 1-\alpha$ for all $y$

nodes.name: Conformal Risk Control
nodes.statement: If $(X_i,Y_i)$ and $(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are i.i.d. and $\ell$ is monotone in $\lambda$ with $\ell(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda_1}(x),y) \geq \ell(\mathcal{C}_{\lambda_2}(x),y)$ for $\lambda_1 \leq \lambda_2$, then $\mathbb{E}[\ell(\mathcal{C}_{\hat{\lambda}}(X_{\rm test}),Y_{\rm test})] \leq \alpha$.

nodes.name: Error control for outlier detection
nodes.statement: If $X_1,\dots,X_n,X_{\rm test}$ are i.i.d. and $\mathcal{C}(x)$ flags $x$ as outlier when $s(x) > \hat{q}$, then $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) = \text{outlier}) \leq \alpha$.

nodes.name: Conformal prediction under covariate shift
nodes.statement: If $(X_i,Y_i) \sim \mathcal{P} \times \mathcal{P}_{Y|X}$ i.i.d. and $(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test}) \sim \mathcal{P}_{\rm test} \times \mathcal{P}_{Y|X}$, then the weighted conformal $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})) \geq 1-\alpha$.
assumptions: $\hat{q}(x)$ computed via weighted quantile with $p_i^w(x), p_{\rm test}^w(x)$

nodes.name: Conformal prediction under distribution drift (TV bound)
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon_i = \mathrm{d}_{\rm TV}((X_i,Y_i),(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test}))$. The weighted conformal $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})) \geq 1-\alpha-2\sum_i \tilde{w}_i\epsilon_i$.
assumptions: Calibration data drawn independently from possibly different distributions $\{\mathcal{P}_i\}_{i=1}^n$

nodes.name: Selective accuracy guarantee
nodes.statement: If $\{(X_i,Y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ and $(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are i.i.d. and $\hat{\lambda}$ is chosen via the upper-bound scan, then $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} = \widehat{Y}(X_{\rm test}) \mid \widehat{P}(X_{\rm test}) \geq \hat{\lambda}) \geq 1-\alpha$ holds with probability $1-\delta$.

nodes.name: Full conformal coverage guarantee
nodes.statement: If $(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_{n+1},Y_{n+1})$ are i.i.d. from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\hat{f}$ is a symmetric (permutation-invariant) algorithm, then the full conformal set $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies $\mathbb{P}(Y_{n+1} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{n+1})) \geq 1-\alpha$.

nodes.name: Learn then Test FWER guarantee
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 Instructions for Learn then Test
nodes.statement: The set $\hat{\Lambda}$ returned by the LTT procedure satisfies $\mathbb{P}(\sup_{\hat{\lambda} \in \hat{\Lambda}} R(\hat{\lambda}) \leq \alpha) \geq 1-\delta$, so any $\hat{\lambda} \in \hat{\Lambda}$ yields an $(\alpha,\delta)$-RCP.
assumptions: For each $\lambda \in \Lambda$, a valid p-value $p_\lambda$ for $\mathcal{H}_\lambda : R(\lambda) > \alpha$

nodes.name: Split conformal prediction
nodes.statement: Given a fitted model $\hat{f}$ and calibration data, compute scores, take the empirical $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n$ quantile $\hat{q}$, and return $\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) = \{y : s(X_{\rm test},y) \leq \hat{q}\}$.
output: Threshold $\hat{q}$ and prediction-set function $\mathcal{C}(\cdot)$ satisfying $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})) \geq 1-\alpha$

nodes.name: Adaptive Prediction Sets (APS)
nodes.statement: Conformal classification using the cumulative-softmax score $s(x,y)=\sum_{j=1}^k \hat{f}(x)_{\pi_j(x)}$ to build adaptive prediction sets that include classes greedily until the cumulative mass exceeds $\hat{q}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Romano et al. 2020; Angelopoulos et al. 2020 (RAPS)

nodes.name: Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR)
nodes.statement: Train quantile regressors $\hat{t}_{\alpha/2},\hat{t}_{1-\alpha/2}$, take score $s(x,y)=\max(\hat{t}_{\alpha/2}(x)-y,\,y-\hat{t}_{1-\alpha/2}(x))$, and inflate the quantile band by $\hat{q}$.

nodes.name: Conformalized scalar uncertainty
nodes.statement: Given point predictor $\hat{f}$ and uncertainty scalar $u(x)$, conformalize the score $s(x,y)=|y-\hat{f}(x)|/u(x)$ to obtain $\mathcal{C}(x) = [\hat{f}(x) \pm u(x)\hat{q}]$.
input: Predictor $\hat{f}$ and uncertainty scalar $u(x)$ (e.g. $\hat{\sigma}$ or residual model)

nodes.name: Conformalized Bayes
nodes.statement: Use posterior predictive density as a score, $s(x,y) = -\hat{f}(y \mid x)$, then form the conformal set $\mathcal{C}(x) = \{y : \hat{f}(y \mid x) > -\hat{q}\}$, achieving Bayes-optimal size among $1-\alpha$ prediction sets.

nodes.name: Group-balanced conformal prediction
nodes.statement: Run split conformal separately within each group $g$ to compute $\hat{q}^{(g)}$, then for input $x$ in group $x_1$ return $\mathcal{C}(x) = \{y : s(x,y) \leq \hat{q}^{(x_1)}\}$.
output: Per-group thresholds $\hat{q}^{(g)}$ and group-conditional prediction set $\mathcal{C}(x)$

nodes.name: Class-conditional conformal prediction
nodes.statement: Stratify scores by class $k$, compute $\hat{q}^{(k)}$ within each class, then include $y$ in $\mathcal{C}(x)$ iff $s(x,y) \leq \hat{q}^{(y)}$.
output: Per-class thresholds $\hat{q}^{(k)}$ and class-conditional prediction set $\mathcal{C}(x)$

nodes.name: Conformal Risk Control (CRC)
nodes.statement: Pick $\hat{\lambda} = \inf\{\lambda : \hat{R}(\lambda) \leq \alpha-\frac{B-\alpha}{n}\}$ on the empirical risk so that the expected loss $\mathbb{E}[\ell(\mathcal{C}_{\hat{\lambda}}(X),Y)] \leq \alpha$.
input: Family of nested predictors $\mathcal{C}_\lambda$ monotone in $\lambda$

nodes.name: Conformal outlier detection
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat{q}$ as the $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n$ quantile of clean-data scores; flag $X_{\rm test}$ as outlier when $s(X_{\rm test}) > \hat{q}$.

nodes.name: Weighted conformal prediction (covariate shift)
nodes.statement: Define test-dependent weights $p_i^w(x), p_{\rm test}^w(x)$ from likelihood ratio $w$, take a reweighted $1-\alpha$ quantile $\hat{q}(x)$, and return $\mathcal{C}(x) = \{y : s(x,y) \leq \hat{q}(x)\}$.

nodes.name: Weighted conformal prediction (distribution drift)
nodes.statement: Use a weight schedule $w_1,\dots,w_n$ (e.g. rolling window or exponential decay) to compute the weighted quantile $\hat{q}$ and the standard set $\mathcal{C}(x) = \{y : s(x,y) \leq \hat{q}\}$.
input: Weight schedule $w_i \in [0,1]$ (e.g. fixed window $\mathbf{1}\{i \geq n-K\}$ or decay $0.99^{n-i+1}$)

nodes.name: Full (transductive) conformal prediction
nodes.statement: For each candidate $y \in \mathcal{Y}$, refit a symmetric model on the augmented dataset, compute scores, and include $y$ in $\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})$ iff $s_{n+1}^y \leq \hat{q}^y$.

nodes.name: Selective classification via Learn then Test
nodes.statement: Scan a Binomial upper bound $\hat{R}^+(\lambda)$ on the selective misclassification rate and pick $\hat{\lambda}$ as the smallest $\lambda$ such that $\hat{R}^+(\lambda') \leq \alpha$ for all $\lambda' \geq \lambda$.
output: Threshold $\hat{\lambda}$ such that $\mathbb{P}(Y_{\rm test}=\widehat{Y}(X_{\rm test}) \mid \widehat{P}(X_{\rm test}) \geq \hat{\lambda}) \geq 1-\alpha$ w.p. $1-\delta$

nodes.name: Learn then Test (LTT)
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 Instructions for Learn then Test
nodes.statement: Form a null $\mathcal{H}_\lambda : R(\lambda) > \alpha$ for each $\lambda \in \Lambda$, compute valid p-values $p_\lambda$ on calibration data, and apply a FWER-controlling algorithm to obtain $\hat{\Lambda}$.
output: Set $\hat{\Lambda}$ of risk-controlling parameters with $(\alpha,\delta)$ guarantee

nodes.name: Bonferroni correction
nodes.section: Appendix A.1.2 Crash Course on FWER
nodes.statement: Return $\hat{\Lambda}_{\rm Bonferroni} = \{\lambda : p_\lambda \leq \delta/|\Lambda|\}$, controlling FWER at level $\delta$ by union bound.

nodes.name: Fixed-sequence testing
nodes.section: Appendix A.1.2 Crash Course on FWER
nodes.statement: Order hypotheses $\{\mathcal{H}_{\lambda_j}\}_{j=1}^N$ a-priori from most- to least-promising; test sequentially at level $\delta$ and stop at first acceptance: $\hat{\Lambda}_{\rm FST} = \{\lambda_j, j \leq T\}$ with $T = \max\{t : p_{\lambda_{t'}} \leq \delta\,\forall t' \leq t\}$.
output: Selected $\hat{\Lambda}_{\rm FST}$ controlling FWER at level $\delta$

nodes.name: ImageNet image-classification with split conformal
nodes.statement: Apply split conformal with score $s_i = 1-\hat{f}(X_i)_{Y_i}$ to ImageNet, producing 1-$\alpha$ prediction sets like in Figure 1 (fox squirrel sets).

nodes.name: MEPS conformalized quantile regression
nodes.statement: CQR applied to the MEPS healthcare-expenditure dataset (notebook meps-cqr) yields conformalized prediction intervals for medical expenditures.

nodes.name: MS-COCO multilabel FNR control
nodes.statement: Use conformal risk control with $\ell_{\rm FNR}(\mathcal{C}_\lambda(x),y) = 1-|\mathcal{C}_\lambda(x)\cap y|/|y|$ on MS-COCO to bound the false-negative rate at $\alpha=0.1$.

nodes.name: Tumor-segmentation FNR control
nodes.statement: Apply conformal risk control with the FNR loss to gut-polyp segmentation masks, guaranteeing $\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\rm FNR}] \leq \alpha$ over missed tumor pixels.

nodes.name: Yandex weather time-series prediction
nodes.section: 5.3 Weather Prediction with Time-Series Distribution Shift
nodes.statement: Use weighted conformal with a fixed-$K$ window on the Yandex Shifts weather dataset and CatBoost ensembles to track temperature in degrees Celsius across an in/out-of-distribution change point.

nodes.name: Toxic-text outlier detection
nodes.statement: Apply outlier-detection conformal with a Detoxify BERT model on the Jigsaw multilingual toxic comments dataset; flags $70\%$ of toxic comments at $\alpha=0.1$.

nodes.name: ImageNet selective classification
nodes.statement: Run the selective-classification LTT special case on ImageNet at $\alpha=0.1$ to abstain on uncertain inputs and achieve higher accuracy than the base model.

nodes.name: MS-COCO multilabel FDR control
nodes.section: Appendix B.1 Multi-label Classification with FDR Control
nodes.statement: Apply LTT with the FDR risk $R_{\rm FDR}(\lambda) = \mathbb{E}[1-|Y\cap \mathcal{T}_\lambda(X)|/|\mathcal{T}_\lambda(X)|]$ on MS-COCO at $\alpha=\delta=0.1$ using fixed-sequence testing and HB p-values.

nodes.name: Simultaneous OOD detection + coverage
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Simultaneous Guarantees on OOD Detection and Coverage
nodes.statement: LTT with two risks ($R_1$ false flag rate, $R_2$ conditional miscoverage) and a 2-D parameter $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$; control both at $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(0.05,0.1)$ via composite p-value $p_\lambda = \max(p_\lambda^{(1)},p_\lambda^{(2)})$.

nodes.name: Score function determines usefulness
nodes.statement: Although conformal prediction's coverage guarantee always holds, the usefulness (size) of the prediction sets is primarily determined by the score function, not by the coverage proof.

nodes.name: Conditional coverage impossibility
nodes.statement: In the most general (continuous-distribution) case, exact conditional coverage is impossible to achieve in a distribution-free way; conformal procedures only approximate it.
nodes.origin_citation: Vovk 2012; Lei & Wasserman 2014; Foygel-Barber et al. 2021

nodes.name: n=1000 calibration heuristic
nodes.section: 3.2 Effect of the Size of the Calibration Set
nodes.statement: From the Beta distribution of coverage, $n=1000$ calibration points typically yields realised coverage in $[0.88, 0.92]$ at $\alpha=0.1$, justifying the rule-of-thumb $n \approx 1000$.

nodes.name: Cost of weighting: effective sample size
nodes.statement: Weighted conformal prediction has variance scaling like $1/\sqrt{n^{\rm eff}}$ where $n^{\rm eff} = (\sum w_i)^2/\sum w_i^2$, so aggressive down-weighting can blow up the coverage variance.

nodes.name: Permutation-test interpretation of full conformal
nodes.statement: $s_{n+1}^y \leq \hat{q}^y$ is exactly the acceptance condition of a level-$\alpha$ permutation test for exchangeability of the augmented score sequence; the conformal set is the set of $y$ accepted by this test.

nodes.name: Proof of conformal coverage guarantee
nodes.statement: By exchangeability, $s_{\rm test}$ is equally likely to fall into any rank position among $s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{\rm test}$, so $P(s_{\rm test} \leq s_{\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil}) = \lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/(n+1) \geq 1-\alpha$.

nodes.name: Reduce to non-trivial case
nodes.statement: Assume scores are distinct (continuous distribution); WLOG sort $s_1<\dots<s_n$. If $\alpha<\frac{1}{n+1}$ then $\hat{q}=\infty$ and $\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})=\mathcal{Y}$, trivially covering.

nodes.name: Identify the coverage event with a score-rank event
nodes.statement: $\{Y_{\rm test} \in \mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test})\} = \{s_{\rm test} \leq \hat{q}\} = \{s_{\rm test} \leq s_{\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil}\}$, using $\hat{q} = s_{\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil}$.

nodes.name: Apply exchangeability
nodes.statement: By exchangeability of $(s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{\rm test})$, $P(s_{\rm test} \leq s_k) = k/(n+1)$ for any integer $k$.

nodes.name: Conclude coverage bound
nodes.statement: Setting $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$ gives $P(s_{\rm test} \leq s_{\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil}) = \lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/(n+1) \geq 1-\alpha$.

nodes.name: Identify heuristic uncertainty
nodes.statement: Identify a heuristic notion of uncertainty using the pre-trained model $\hat{f}$ (e.g. softmax outputs, residuals, $\hat{\sigma}$).

nodes.name: Define score function
nodes.statement: Define the score function $s(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}$ where larger scores encode worse agreement between $x$ and $y$.

nodes.name: Compute conformal quantile
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat{q}$ as the $\frac{\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil}{n}$ empirical quantile of calibration scores $s_1,\dots,s_n$.

nodes.name: Form prediction set
nodes.statement: Return $\mathcal{C}(X_{\rm test}) = \{y : s(X_{\rm test},y) \leq \hat{q}\}$.

nodes.name: Sort softmax outputs
nodes.statement: Compute the permutation $\pi(x)$ that sorts $\hat{f}(x)$ from most likely to least likely class.

nodes.name: Cumulative-mass score
nodes.statement: Define $s(x,y) = \sum_{j=1}^k \hat{f}(x)_{\pi_j(x)}$ where $y = \pi_k(x)$, the cumulative softmax mass up to the true label.

nodes.name: Calibrate quantile
nodes.statement: Set $\hat{q} = \mathrm{Quantile}(s_1,\dots,s_n; \lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n)$.

nodes.name: Form adaptive prediction set
nodes.statement: Return $\mathcal{C}(x) = \{\pi_1(x),\dots,\pi_k(x)\}$ where $k = \sup\{k' : \sum_{j=1}^{k'} \hat{f}(x)_{\pi_j(x)} < \hat{q}\} + 1$.

nodes.name: Loop over candidate labels
nodes.statement: For each $y \in \mathcal{Y}$, refit a symmetric model $\hat{f}^y$ on the augmented dataset $(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_{n+1},y)$.

nodes.name: Compute per-$y$ scores
nodes.statement: Compute $s_i^y = s(X_i,Y_i,\hat{f}^y)$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ and $s_{n+1}^y = s(X_{n+1},y,\hat{f}^y)$.

nodes.name: Compute per-$y$ quantile
nodes.statement: Set $\hat{q}^y = \mathrm{Quantile}(s_1^y,\dots,s_n^y; \lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n)$.

nodes.name: Collect consistent labels
nodes.statement: Return $\mathcal{C}(X_{n+1}) = \{y : s_{n+1}^y \leq \hat{q}^y\}$, the set of $y$ consistent with the calibration scores.

nodes.name: Form null hypotheses
nodes.statement: For each $\lambda \in \Lambda$, associate the null $\mathcal{H}_\lambda : R(\lambda) > \alpha$; rejecting it means selecting $\lambda$ as risk-controlled.

nodes.name: Compute p-values
nodes.statement: For each $\mathcal{H}_\lambda$ compute a valid p-value via concentration (e.g. Hoeffding $p_\lambda = e^{-2n(\alpha-\hat{R}(\lambda))_+^2}$ or HB).

nodes.name: Apply FWER algorithm
nodes.statement: Return $\hat{\Lambda} = \mathcal{A}(\{p_\lambda\})$ where $\mathcal{A}$ controls FWER (e.g. Bonferroni: $\hat{\Lambda} = \{\lambda : p_\lambda < \delta/|\Lambda|\}$).
